\begin{theorem}[Input copy machine run]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.inputCall_copy}
\label{Turing.FinTM.inputCall_copy}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nil, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.inputCopyTM, Turing.inputCopyTM_run_ofCfg, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{4}
Let $k>0$ and let $x$ be a Boolean word. Starting with the input-copy machine's sweep
state, its input head at the first input position, all work tapes empty with their heads
at the origin, and empty output, after $2|x|+2$ steps the machine is in the done state
with $x$ on work tape $0$, every other work tape empty, all work-tape heads at the
origin, and the input head and output tape as in the standard word configuration.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Input call machine]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.exists_inputCallTM}
\label{Turing.FinTM.exists_inputCallTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.exists_installCallTM, Turing.FinTM.inputCall_copy, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.SweepPhase, Turing.inputCopyTM, Turing.inputCopyTM_run_ofCfg, Turing.seamCompTM, Turing.seamCompTM_firstReturn_ofCfg, Turing.seamCompTM_run_ofCfg, Turing.seamReleaseTM, Turing.seamReleaseTM_firstReturn, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{6}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over Boolean words, let $f$ map Boolean words to
Boolean words, and let $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. Suppose $M$ computes $f$
within $T(|x|)$ steps on every input $x$. Then there are a finite Turing machine $C$,
entry and exit states of $C$, and a natural number $c$ with at least one work tape, such
that for every input $x$, starting from the clean seam in the entry state with all work
tapes blank, there is a positive time $t\le c(T(|x|)+|x|+|f(x)|+1)$ at which $C$
reaches the clean seam in the exit state with $f(x)$ on its first work tape and all
other work tapes blank; the exit state is not visited at any earlier positive time
before $t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Input rewind states]
\lean{Turing.InputSeekRw}
\label{Turing.InputSeekRw}
\leanok
The input rewind procedure has four states: a start state, a scanning state, a
leftward-return state, and a done state.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Input seek and rewind machine]
\lean{Turing.inputSeekRewind}
\label{Turing.inputSeekRewind}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.InputSeekRw, Turing.MultiTapeTM}
There is a deterministic Turing machine with two work tapes, Boolean symbols, and states
`start`, `scan`, `left`, and `done`. It starts in `start`; in `start` it moves the input
head left and enters `scan`; in `scan` it moves left and remains in `scan` when the
scanned input symbol is present, and moves right and enters `left` when it is blank; in
`left` it moves left and enters `done`; in `done` it stays in place and remains in
`done`.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Input seek and rewind run]
\lean{Turing.inputSeekRewind_run}
\label{Turing.inputSeekRewind_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.FinTM.controlAction_apply, Turing.FinTM.moveInputPos_neg_val, Turing.FinTM.rewind_heads, Turing.InputSeekRw, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.inputSeekRewind, Turing.step_of_inputMoveAction}
\difficulty{6}
Let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $d$ be a configuration of the
input-seek-and-rewind machine on input $x$ whose state is start. Writing $p(d)$ for the
position of its input head, there is a time $r\le p(d)+3$ at which the machine is in
state done with its input head at position $0$; it is not in state done at any earlier
time $u<r$, and both work-tape head positions agree with those of $d$ at every time
$u\le r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[One-step input seek machine]
\lean{Turing.inputSeekStep}
\label{Turing.inputSeekStep}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.inputMoveAction}
There is a deterministic Turing machine with one work tape, Boolean symbols, and a
single state, which it uses as its initial state. At every step, regardless of the
scanned input symbol or work-tape contents, its transition is the action that moves the
input head one step to the right and keeps the machine in that state.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Input head seek run]
\lean{Turing.inputSeekStep_run}
\label{Turing.inputSeekStep_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.inputSeekStep, Turing.moveInputPos, Turing.step_of_inputMoveAction}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ be a finite Boolean input, and let $c$ be a configuration of the one-work-tape
machine `inputSeekStep` whose state is the active state. After any $r\in\mathbb{N}$
steps from $c$, the resulting configuration agrees with $c$ in every component except
the input-head position, which is obtained by moving the head one position to the right,
with boundary clamping, exactly $r$ times.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Rightward input head position]
\lean{Turing.inputSeek_right_value}
\label{Turing.inputSeek_right_value}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.moveInputPos, Turing.moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,r\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $p$ be one of the $n+2$ input-head positions. If $p+r\le
n+1$, then moving the head one position to the right, with boundary clamping, $r$ times
from $p$ yields position $p+r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Composed input-seeking machine]
\lean{Turing.inputSeekMachine}
\label{Turing.inputSeekMachine}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CounterLoopState, Turing.InputSeekRw, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.SweepPhase, Turing.clearTM, Turing.copyTM, Turing.counterLoopTM, Turing.inputSeekRewind, Turing.inputSeekStep, Turing.seamCompTM}
There is a deterministic Turing machine with two work tapes and Boolean symbols. Its
state set is the disjoint union of the sweep phases, the four input-rewind states, the
counter-loop states with unit body state, and another copy of the sweep phases; its
transition function is the composition of the two-tape copy machine, the
input-seeking-and-rewind machine, the counter loop driven by the one-step input-seek
machine, and the tape-clearing machine, joined using the specified exit states.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Work tape range across a seam]
\lean{Turing.inputSeek_seam_range}
\label{Turing.inputSeek_seam_range}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.seamCompTM, Turing.seamCompTM_visitedByTapeHead_ofCfg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be two-tape Turing machines over Boolean symbols, with state sets
$S_1$ and $S_2$, respectively, and choose an exit state $e$ of $M_1$ and an entry state
$a$ of $M_2$. Suppose configurations $c_0,c_1$ of $M_1$ satisfy that running $M_1$ from
$c_0$ for $t_1$ steps gives $c_1$, whose state is $e$, and that no earlier time $u<t_1$
has state $e$. If integer bounds $\ell_j,h_j$ are specified for each of the two work
tapes, and the work-tape head positions of the run of $M_1$ from $c_0$ remain in
$[\ell_j,h_j]$ through time $t_1$, while those of $M_2$ started from $c_1$ with its
state renamed to $a$ remain in those intervals through time $t_2$, then the work-tape
head positions of the composite machine run from $c_0$ with its state renamed to the
left component remain in the same intervals through time $t_1+1+t_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Machine seeking an input position]
\lean{Turing.exists_inputSeekTM}
\label{Turing.exists_inputSeekTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.CounterLoopState, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.InputSeekRw, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.SweepPhase, Turing.clearTM, Turing.clearTM_run_ofCfg, Turing.copyTM, Turing.copyTM_run_ofCfg, Turing.counterLoopCfg, Turing.counterLoopOrbit, Turing.counterLoopTM, Turing.counterLoopTM_run_done, Turing.counterOverhead, Turing.counterOverhead_le, Turing.counter_cfg_eq, Turing.inputSeekMachine, Turing.inputSeekRewind, Turing.inputSeekRewind_run, Turing.inputSeekStep, Turing.inputSeekStep_run, Turing.inputSeek_right_value, Turing.inputSeek_seam_range, Turing.seamCompTM, Turing.seamCompTM_firstReturn_ofCfg, Turing.seamCompTM_run_ofCfg}
\difficulty{7}
There exist a finite state set, a deterministic Turing machine with two work tapes over
the Boolean alphabet, entry and exit states, and a natural-number constant $C$ with the
following property. For every Boolean input word $x$, natural number $p$, and Boolean
word $w$ such that the base-two value of the digits of $w$ is $p$ and $p\le |x|+1$,
consider any configuration $d$ on input $x$ whose state is the entry state, whose first
work tape agrees with the tape storing $w$ from one cell to the left of its head through
one cell beyond the word (and is blank elsewhere), and whose second work tape is blank
everywhere. There is a time $t\le C(|w|+s+p+1)$, where $s$ is the input-head position in
$d$, such that the machine is not in the exit state at any earlier time, and at time $t$
it is in the exit state with input-head position $p$. At every time $u\le t$, each
work-tape head has moved from its initial position by at most $C(|w|+1)$, and at time
$t$ both work tapes, both work-tape head positions, and the output word are unchanged
from $d$.
\end{theorem}
